newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian lawmaker kidnapped by rebels drowns.
newsitem.headline: Colombian lawmaker kidnapped by rebels drowns.

text.p: A former ruling party legislator, held captive by leftist guerrillas for almost two years, drowned in a river in southern Colombia over the weekend as he was being taken to another hideout, police said on Monday.
Rodrigo Turbay, 37, was abducted by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) insurgents in southern Caqueta province in June 1995 on suspicion of stealing public funds.

In a short statement sent to a radio station in Caqueta, the FARC said Turbay drowned late Saturday when the boat in which rebels were moving him from one hideout to another capsized. Police said his body was washed ashore Sunday afternoon.

Turbay, from a powerful family of Caqueta politicians, was stripped of his post as Liberal Party representative in the lower chamber of Congress because of his alleged links with known drug traffickers shortly before his kidnap.

In a separate incident over the weekend, six rebels of the National Liberation Army ELN, Colombia's second largest rebel force, died in a firefight with government troops in northwest Antioquia province, regional commander Gen. Rafael Hernandez said. One soldier was also killed.
